newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's 1996 public sector foreign debt up.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's 1996 public sector foreign debt up.

text.p: Colombia's public sector foreign debt grew 8.83 percent to $16.4 billion in 1996, the central bank said in a report issued Monday.
Total foreign debt, including the private sector, rose 10.9 percent from 1995 to $27.3 billion, the report said.
The government originally planned to contract a further $1.96 billion in foreign debt this year but slashed those estimates by $800 million following a sharp influx of dollars in December.
Under the terms of its state of economic emergency decreed two weeks ago, the government cut the net public sector foreign debt to $1.2 billion for 1997.
It also clamped a new six percent tax on newly contracted public and private foreign debt in a bid to encourage domestic borrowing.

According to Finance Ministry figures, the cost of servicing the central government foreign debt rose 23 percent to about $471 million in 1996 compared with the previous year but remained stable when taken as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product at 0.53 percent.
The increase in the cost of debt servicing contributed to the yawning fiscal deficit, which hit 4.11 percent of GDP in 1996.
